human_understanding_delta: The collar/slack producer was asking for upper semicontinuity of the two-root lemniscate path length Lam, which negative_results entry 3 shows has no uniform modulus. The reduction only ever needed lower semicontinuity, and that is free: roots in the closed unit disk force every sublevel set into the fixed disk |z|<=2, so bounded-length paths for a convergent sequence of polynomials are equi-Lipschitz in a fixed compact set and Arzela-Ascoli plus lower semicontinuity of length transports a path to the limit. Hence {Lam<=2} is closed and any dense subclass suffices. Combined with the already-recorded minimum-enclosing-disk normalisation, which supplies both strict inequalities from R<1 and spends no slack, the unrestricted problem in degree n becomes the single extremal statement that z^n-1 maximises Lam on the compact closed-disk class, with Lam(z^n-1)=2 proved exactly by the petal split.
